subject: [PATCH v2 2/4] mm: don't PTE-batch a swap-in of a folio with a hardware-poisoned page

reviews.author: Joshua Hahn
reviews.summary: Joshua approved the patch with a Reviewed-by tag, indicating that he thinks it is correct and suitable for inclusion in the kernel.
reviews.raw_body:
On Sun, Nov 15, 2026 at 10:34:56PM -0800, Usama Arif wrote:
> do_swap_page() checks PageHWPoison() on the faulting page, but the
> large-folio batching path then maps the rest of the folio without
> looking at its other pages. A poisoned page that is not the one being
> faulted gets mapped anyway, and the fault that would have reported it
> never happens.
> 
> Skip batching for such an anon folio and let each page take its own
> fault, where the existing check catches it. do_set_pmd() already backs
> off the same way.
> 
> Leave a freshly read folio alone: it is not anon yet and can only be
> mapped as a whole, and falling back would free it with the poisoned
> page still in it, which the retried fault can then get back from the
> page allocator.

LGTM!

Reviewed-by: Joshua Hahn <joshua.hahnjy@gmail.com>

> Fixes: 508758960b8d ("mm: swap: entirely map large folios found in swapcache")
> Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
> Signed-off-by: Usama Arif <usama.arif@linux.dev>
> ---
>  mm/memory.c | 5 +++++
>  1 file changed, 5 insertions(+)
> 
> diff --git a/mm/memory.c b/mm/memory.c
> index d477a4f986bc8..51e72fb40655f 100644
> --- a/mm/memory.c
> +++ b/mm/memory.c
> @@ -5158,6 +5158,11 @@ vm_fault_t do_swap_page(struct vm_fault *vmf)
>  		    swap_pte_batch(folio_ptep, nr, folio_pte) != nr)
>  			goto check_folio;
>  
> +		/* A poisoned page in the folio must take its own fault. */
> +		if (folio_test_anon(folio) &&
> +		    folio_contain_hwpoisoned_page(folio))
> +			goto check_folio;
> +
>  		page_idx = idx;
>  		address = folio_start;
>  		ptep = folio_ptep;
> -- 
> 2.53.1-Meta
>

reviews.author: David Hildenbrand
reviews.summary: David suggested moving the check for poisoned pages before calling swap_pte_batch(), which would prevent the mapping of poisoned pages.

reviews.author: Zi Yan
reviews.summary: Zi agreed with David's suggestion and proposed moving the check before folio_pte_range(). He also added a Reviewed-by tag.

> Leave a freshly read folio alone: it is not anon yet and can only be

reviews.summary: Kiryl pointed out a potential issue with file-side handling of large folios and suggested adding a check in finish_fault(). He also added a Reviewed-by tag.

2026-11-16.patch_summary: This patch series addresses a bug in the Linux kernel's memory management, specifically when handling large folios (memory allocations) that contain hardware-poisoned pages. The problem arises from the fact that the PTE-batching path does not check for poisoned pages before mapping them. This can lead to unexpected behavior and potential crashes. The patch series proposes a fix by adding checks to ensure that each page in the folio takes its own fault, preventing the mapping of poisoned pages.
